Currently
column2: the HV KVM guest entry/exit code adds the timebase offset

column1: from the vcore struct to the timebase on guest entry
it on guest exit.  Which is fine
column2: except that it is possible for

column1: userspace to change the offset using the SET_ONE_REG interface while
the vcore is running
column2: as there is only one timebase offset per vcore

column1: but potentially multiple VCPUs in the vcore.  If that were to happen
KVM would subtract a different offset on guest exit from that which
it had added on guest entry
column2: leading to the timebase being out of sync

column1: between cores in the host
column2: which then leads to bad things happening

column1: such as hangs and spurious watchdog timeouts.
To fix this
column2: we add a new field 'tb_offset_applied' to the vcore struct

column1: which stores the offset that is currently applied to the timebase.
This value is set from the vcore tb_offset field on guest entry
is what is subtracted from the timebase on guest exit.  Since it is
zero when the timebase offset is not applied
logic in kvmhv_start_timing and kvmhv_accumulate_time.
In addition
column2: we had secondary threads reading the timebase while

column1: running concurrently with code on the primary thread which would
eventually add or subtract the timebase offset from the timebase.
This occurred while saving or restoring the DEC register value on
the secondary threads.  Although no specific incorrect behaviour has
been observed
column2: this is a race which should be fixed.  To fix it

column1: move the DEC saving code to just before we call kvmhv_commence_exit
and the DEC restoring code to after the point where we have waited
for the primary thread to switch the MMU context and add the timebase
